headline: Two unbeaten runs end and Monaco stay narrow favourites
summary: Both unbeaten starts ended on Sunday. Monaco lost 0-1 at Lorient; Freiburg went down 1-2 at Bayer Leverkusen. On Thursday they meet in the Conference League, both with a win from their opening game. Freiburg have created more — 1.98 expected goals per game over their last five, against Monaco's 1.18 — but they also lose defender Philipp Lienhart, SWR reports. Even so, the market makes Monaco 41.8% favourites and rates them only 0.25 goals better. Freiburg are at 31.3%.
read: Monaco are narrow home favourites against a Freiburg side whose chance creation over the last five games has been clearly the better of the two.

facts.fact: Monaco are the market's favourites at 41.8% to win, against Freiburg's 31.3%.
Freiburg have averaged 1.98 xG per game over their last five, against Monaco's 1.18.
facts.meaning: Freiburg create nearly a goal more in chance quality per game, which is why this is no walkover for the home side.

facts.fact: Freiburg defender Philipp Lienhart will miss the match through load management, a club spokesperson confirmed.
facts.meaning: Freiburg lose a regular at the back for a game against a home side that needs a result.

facts.fact: Monaco lost 0-1 at Lorient on Sunday, ending their run as Ligue 1's last unbeaten side.
facts.meaning: Their first league defeat of the season came with only 0.6 xG created — the home side arrives short of attacking rhythm.

facts.fact: Freiburg lost 1-2 at Bayer Leverkusen on Sunday, their first Bundesliga defeat of the season.
facts.meaning: The unbeaten start is over, but 1.21 xG away at Leverkusen was no collapse.

facts.fact: Eric Dier and Stanis Idumbo are out for Monaco, with the club reporting no new injuries.
facts.meaning: Both ends of the squad are thinned slightly, but Monaco go into the game with an otherwise settled group.

facts.fact: Both teams to score is priced at 58.9% — more likely than not.
facts.meaning: The market expects both defences to be beaten, even with a modest goal expectation for the match.

facts.fact: Both sides won their opening Conference League match and sit level on 3 points, Freiburg 7th and Monaco 9th of 36.

sources.fact: Eric Dier and Stanis Idumbo are out for Monaco's Conference League tie against Freiburg.
Monaco have three players out but no new injuries ahead of hosting Freiburg.
Monaco lost 1-0 at Lorient, ending their status as the only unbeaten team in Ligue 1.
Monaco manager Filipe Luís said of the favourites tag: "Favourites? I don't think so… you only win titles in May and June."
Filipe Luís said: "We will just think about this one. We have to try and win tomorrow. That is the main goal."
Freiburg defender Philipp Lienhart will miss the Monaco game due to load management, per a club spokesperson.
Freiburg lost their first Bundesliga game of the season, 2-1 at Bayer Leverkusen, ending their unbeaten start.
Freiburg had started excellently in all competitions this season, losing just once under Julian Schuster, according to Yahoo Sports.
